Stage 1 of our journey · Real pump data

The first prototype: 15 days of real pump data

Our first step used a real export of pump records from 579 Bengaluru borewells, covering 15–29 July 2026. It proved the data could be turned into forecasts. Fifteen days is far too short to forecast months ahead, which is why later stages exist.

What you can do here

Pick a well and a time span. The page shows where that well's water was last measured and a rough what-if for the future.

Read the range, not the line

With only 15 days of data, the shaded range is deliberately wide. For long spans it mostly shows how uncertain the future is.

What this stage proved

Pump records can be cleaned and linked to water levels. Short-term changes during pumping were predictable to within about 9 m on raw records. See the full story.

Choose a well

Anonymised IDs from BW001 to BW579. Start typing to see the list.

A what-if lever: more pumping pushes the water deeper.

Keep in mind

Borewell Forecast is a proof of concept for forecasting groundwater levels in Bengaluru borewells. Results are labelled by where the data came from: real pump data (15 days, July 2026), synthetic test system (450 simulated wells with a known answer) or digital twin (a physics-based simulation of the 579 wells over a year). Nothing here is yet a validated field forecast.
